title: `_acquire_lock` is a non-atomic check-then-set and its release has no ownership token
what_is_wrong: `get` followed by `set` is two round trips, so two workers can both observe an empty key and both proceed, and `set` followed by a separate `expire` leaves a permanent lock if the process dies between them; the release deletes the key unconditionally, including when it now belongs to a different worker.

title: `_acquire_lock` is a non-atomic check-then-set and releases a lock it may no longer own
what_is_wrong: `get` then `set` then `expire` is three round trips with no atomicity, so two workers can both observe an absent key and both proceed; and the unconditional `delete` in `finally` removes whatever value is at `LOCK_KEY`, including a lock a *different* worker acquired after this one's TTL expired.

title: `_acquire_lock` is a non-atomic check-then-set, and the release deletes whoever holds the lock
what_is_wrong: `get` followed by `set` is a TOCTOU window two workers both pass (R5 applied to a non-transactional store), `set` followed by a separate `expire` leaves the key with no TTL if the process dies between them, and the release deletes `LOCK_KEY` unconditionally without checking that this worker still owns it.

title: `_acquire_lock` is not a lock — get-then-set is not atomic, and release is unconditional
what_is_wrong: the `get`/`set` pair has a window in which two workers both observe an empty key and both proceed; the `set` and `expire` are separate commands so a crash between them leaves the key with no TTL; and the release deletes the key by name without proving ownership, so a worker whose lock already expired deletes the lock a different worker now holds.
